title: The pause before the edit
spec: M04 · plan, inspect, edit, then approve
intro: Adding one query parameter to TaskFlow's task list. Plan Mode splits that into a read phase you can argue with and a write phase you authorise — and the arguing costs ten seconds.

provenance.source: a narrated session against the shipped sample-project/taskflow; file paths, commands and the failure transcript are taken from the module, terminal output is reconstructed

foot: Run it for real: cd sample-project/taskflow && gemini --plan "…"

steps.title: Ask with --plan, and nothing is written
narrative: You want GET /tasks/ to accept a completed_after parameter. Today routers/tasks.py filters on completed, priority and tag — dates are not in the list.
gemini --plan runs Phase 1 only: it reads, it reasons, it emits a numbered plan. Three files are opened. Zero bytes are written. That gap is the entire feature.
steps.youDo: cd sample-project/taskflow, then run gemini --plan with the change you want, referencing @routers/tasks.py.

terminal.text: gemini --plan "Add a completed_after query param (Optional[datetime]) to GET /tasks/ in @routers/tasks.py. Return only tasks where created_at >= completed_after when the param is provided."

Phase 1 complete. 3 files read, 0 files modified.
Drafting a plan.

before.title: AFTER THREE FILE READS — the disk is untouched

cells: the list_tasks signature and existing filter chain

steps.title: Read the plan the way you read a pull request
narrative: Five steps, three reads and two writes, and one of the writes cancels itself: step 5 says schemas.py needs no change because created_at is already on the response model. Gemini worked that out during Phase 1 and left the reasoning in the plan rather than quietly dropping it.

Check three things before you touch the keyboard. Is every file you expect in WRITE? Is anything in WRITE that you did not ask for — main.py, auth.py? Are there EXEC steps, and do you know exactly what would run? Here there are none, which is the answer you want for a filter change.
steps.claudeSays: The plan is text. It has changed nothing and it commits you to nothing until you answer the prompt at the bottom.

terminal.text:
⚙  Gemini Plan — Add completed_after filter to GET /tasks/

  1. READ   routers/tasks.py   understand list_tasks and the current filter pattern
  2. READ   schemas.py         verify Task response includes created_at
  3. READ   models.py          confirm Task.created_at is DateTime
  4. WRITE  routers/tasks.py   add completed_after: Optional[datetime] = Query(None)
                               and .filter(Task.created_at >= completed_after)
  5. WRITE  schemas.py         no change needed — created_at already present (skipping)

  2 files to modify | 3 files to read | 0 shell commands

rows: Add completed_after: Optional[datetime] = Query(None) and .filter(Task.created_at >= completed_after) to list_tasks()
no null check, no datetime import, no Query description

steps.title: Edit one step instead of rejecting the plan
narrative: Step 4 is directionally right and mechanically thin. As written it never says what happens when the parameter is absent, it does not mention the from datetime import datetime the annotation needs, and it leaves the parameter undocumented in the OpenAPI page at /docs.
Answer e, pick step 4, and replace it. This costs about ten seconds. Answering n and re-prompting regenerates the whole plan and re-reads all three files to fix one sentence.
The gotcha: edited steps are not validated. If your replacement contradicts another step, Gemini executes your text literally — so re-read the whole plan after editing, not just the line you touched.
steps.youDo: Answer e at the gate, choose step 4, and paste a tighter version of it.

terminal.text:
Current step 4:
  Add completed_after: Optional[datetime] = Query(None) and
  .filter(Task.created_at >= completed_after) to list_tasks()

Your edit (press Enter to keep current, or type replacement):

Add completed_after: Optional[datetime] = Query(None, description="Filter tasks created after this datetime (UTC ISO-8601)"). Guard it: if completed_after: query = query.filter(Task.created_at >= completed_after). Add the import: from datetime import datetime

state.label: step 4, before and after your edit

rows: with the param absent, completed_after is None and the comparison filters everything out

after.title: AFTER — one step rewritten, plan re-presented

rows: Query(None, description="Filter tasks created after this datetime (UTC ISO-8601)")
appears on the parameter in the generated OpenAPI page
absent param is now a no-op, which is what a filter should do

steps.title: Approve, and watch the plan become a diff
narrative: Answer y. Phase 2 executes the steps in order: three reads, one write, one skip. One file modified — the same file the plan said it would modify, with the wording you supplied.

Toggle Before / After. The left panel is intent; the right panel is the artefact. Because you edited step 4 rather than accepting it, the diff arrives with the guard, the import and the description already in place — three review comments that never had to be written.

Plan Mode is not free. You pay an extra round trip and a decision point on every task, and for a one-line change in a file you already have open that is pure overhead. It earns its keep when the blast radius is uncertain, which is exactly when you are least able to judge it.
steps.youDo: Answer y, then confirm the change: git diff routers/tasks.py
